The part of a tree that grows underground is the root.

The author employs an alternating first-person point of view, allowing the narrative to shift between the perspectives of different members of a space expedition team. This technique provides a multifaceted look at the events, contrasting the optimistic and curious mindset of the scientist with the pragmatic and cautious outlook of the engineer. The tone is dynamic, adapting to the context: it is technical and precise when describing machinery and phenomena, but becomes reflective and philosophical when the characters contemplate their existence and place in the universe.
